$comment: Known-good HMAC-SHA256 signature vectors for Octonomy webhook deliveries. Generated by generate_vectors.py, which mirrors the server's octonomy/events/dispatch.py::_webhook_signature. Portable across SDKs -- see README.md in this directory.
format: sha256=<lowercase hex digest of HMAC-SHA256(utf8(secret), raw_body)>

encoding.secret: UTF-8 text, encoded to bytes before use as the HMAC key
encoding.body: UTF-8 text; when a vector carries body_base64 instead, the body is those base64-decoded BYTES

accept.name: global-tag-created-envelope
accept.description: A real tag.created outbox envelope for the global (tenant-shared) namespace, serialized the way the server serializes it: compact separators, sorted keys, UTF-8.

accept.name: merchant-tag-updated-envelope
accept.description: A merchant-namespaced tag.updated envelope carrying a request_id. *.updated payloads hold only the CHANGED fields, not a full snapshot.

accept.name: rotated-secret
accept.description: The global envelope signed with a second secret. During rotation a consumer must accept a body signed by EITHER secret, so the same body appears here under both.

accept.name: minimal-ascii-body
accept.description: A short all-ASCII body. The floor case: if this one fails, nothing else will pass either.

accept.name: utf8-body
accept.description: A body with multi-byte UTF-8: accented Latin, Greek, CJK, and an emoji outside the BMP. Signing the decoded string instead of its bytes fails here.

accept.name: utf8-secret
accept.description: A secret that is itself multi-byte UTF-8. The key is utf8(secret), not its code points.

accept.name: trailing-newline-body
accept.description: The minimal ASCII body plus one trailing newline -- a different signature. Any implementation that trims, re-serializes, or 'tidies' the body before hashing produces the minimal-ascii-body digest here and is wrong.

accept.name: non-utf8-binary-body
accept.description: A body that is not valid UTF-8 at all (carried as body_base64). HMAC is over bytes; a string-typed body parameter cannot express this case.

reject.name: missing-header
reject.description: No X-Octonomy-Signature header at all -- an unsigned POST to the webhook endpoint.

reject.name: bare-hex-no-prefix
reject.description: The correct digest with the sha256= prefix stripped. Correct bytes, wrong grammar.

reject.name: uppercase-prefix
reject.description: SHA256= rather than sha256=. The server emits lowercase; the prefix is matched exactly.

reject.name: sha512-prefix
reject.description: A digest announced as a different algorithm. Accepting it would let a sender choose the algorithm.

reject.name: non-hex-digest
reject.description: Sixty-four characters that are not hexadecimal.

reject.name: short-digest
reject.description: A hex digest one character short of SHA-256's 64. A length-blind comparison can read this as a prefix match.

reject.name: even-length-short-digest
reject.description: The correct digest with its last TWO characters removed: still valid hex, still decodable, still the wrong length. An implementation that leaves length to the comparison reports this as a mismatch rather than as malformed -- and one that compares only as far as the shorter value accepts it outright.

reject.name: even-length-long-digest
reject.description: The correct digest with two extra hex characters appended -- decodable, and 33 bytes where 32 are required.

reject.name: long-digest
reject.description: The correct digest with an extra hex character appended.

reject.name: empty-digest
reject.description: The prefix with nothing after it.

reject.name: wrong-secret
reject.description: A well-formed digest of this exact body under a DIFFERENT secret -- what an attacker who cannot read the signing secret produces.

reject.name: body-mutated-after-signing
reject.description: The signature is genuine for the original envelope; the body has had one field value changed since. This is the whole reason verification exists.

reject.name: truncated-body
reject.description: A genuine signature over the full envelope, presented with a body cut short -- what a size-capped or partially-read stream hands the verifier.

reject.name: empty-body-consumed-stream
reject.description: A genuine signature over the full envelope, presented with zero bytes -- what a verifier gets when middleware, a logger, or a JSON decoder drained the request body first.

reject.name: empty-body-correct-digest
reject.description: Zero bytes together with their OWN correct digest. Cryptographically this pair is valid -- HMAC of the empty message is well defined -- and it is recorded here so an SDK that chooses to accept empty bodies has the digest. octonomy-go refuses it: the Octonomy server never emits an empty body, so the realistic cause is a drained stream, and 'empty_body' is therefore a POLICY reason rather than a cryptographic one. See README.md.

reject.name: empty-secret
reject.description: A correct digest under an EMPTY signing secret -- what an unset environment variable produces. The digest verifies, which is the danger: with no secret the key is public, so anyone can mint one. Refused as policy, like empty_body.
